stay_athletic_standard.title: What a 'stay athletic and active' (athletic but not competitive) plan contains, in the coach's terms
coach_words: COACH-ANSWER ATH-13: a program 'for weekend warriors: people that wanted to be athletic, but they didn't need to compete in any sport ... non-competitive, all-around athletic adults. Youth can be there too, and kids ... a good mix of everything ... good health all around and just having a body that performs well.'

Coach request 2026-10-08 (relayed in this workflow): gen-pop and general-fitness people want 'things like high rows [HYROX] and pickleball, meaning they want to stay athletic and active, so we need to understand that that's an option for them.'
COACH-ANSWER ATH-10: 'everyone gets Olympic lifts' in athletic training (beginners: DB / KB snatches, hex-bar jumps, hang pulls / cleans).

COACH-R2 ATH-08: older adults - no Olympic lifts, plyos or depth jumps by default, 'an additional option if they want to do it', with 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means.'
stay_athletic_standard.definition: The coach's own non-competitive athletic program (BYOP 'ATHLETIC - FULL BODY - 4 DAYS A', the former 'Justice League' tab, renamed 'Athletic Performance - Non-Competitive') is the template: every main day opens with light core, then a short athletic block (jumps, a throw, a change-of-direction drill, an Olympic lift), then full-body resistance in hip + push / knee + pull pairs, calves and rear delts; optional days carry Focus work and aerobic sessions. Recreational = no position, no season dates, no pre- / in-season blocks (GEN-02); the activity only changes WHICH athletic qualities lead and how much.

per_main_day.dose: 5 min any cardio + A-drills / mobility; never counted as volume
2 exercises x 2 sets, light, short of failure; movable; core supersets / monster sets may be added anywhere

1-2 jump stations x 2 sets; plyometric vs ballistic by the activity's ground-contact class (75 / 60 / 50 / 40 / 25 %), each block 15 points more ballistic at the start; Receive-Create stages 1 Land -> 2 Land & Go -> 3 Repeat
0-1 medball station x 2 sets (more for rotational activities: racket sports, golf); ball <= 20 lb, lighter for youth and older

0-1 change-of-direction station x 2 sets, EASY -> MOD. TURN (HARD TURN and reactive agility for L2+); none needed for linear / grounded activities, but one light footwork station a week keeps 'some agility' (PROPOSED)

1 station x 2 sets on most main days (up to 4 a week): clean variants on squat days, snatch variants on hinge days; L1 = hang clean, KB squat clean, single-arm DB snatch, hex-bar jump, hang pulls; explained as power output, loaded by RIR / RPE
per_main_day.tag: COACH-ANSWER ATH-10; COACH-R2 ATH-04/05, GEN-06, LIB-07

per_main_day.dose: 2-4 exercises per muscle group trained that day (never 1); hip-dominant + push, knee-dominant + pull; cross-pattern pairing; heavy squat and heavy deadlift on different days; volume by the engine: general factor x0.8, floor 10 sets a week per muscle, stairway steps
per_main_day.tag: COACH-ANSWER UNI-06, UNI-11; COACH-R2 SES-01/02/05, VOL-04/06, PER-03/04; 12 v1.1 §3.4

per_main_day.dose: calves 3 sets every leg day; rear delts / KB face pulls their own sets
3 sessions a week - one Blue (A), one Green (B), one Orange (C); the user can add or remove sessions; the activity itself can count (PROPOSED)

how_much_by_days.2_days: 2 main days + the activity: ~4 athletic stations a day (8-10 sets), resistance on the 05 2-day template; aerobic = the activity + 0-1 gym sessions
how_much_by_days.3_days: the default for most activities: 4-5 athletic stations a day (10-14 sets per day at most, often less), resistance on the 05 3-day template (S1 squat / S2 non-axial hinge / S3 deadlift)
how_much_by_days.4_days: the coach's own template (weekend warrior): 2 jumps + 1 throw + 1 COD + 1 Olympic a day (about 10 athletic sets a day), 2 optional days
how_much_by_days.evidence: OBSERVED BYOP athletic slots (OT04) + 05 v1.1 templates; scaling PROPOSED

weekly_ranges.fast_reactive_plyometric_contacts: 0-56 (gen-pop sits below the coach's field-athlete bands; 60+ default 0 beyond low ankle hops)
weekly_ranges.throws: 0-80 (rotational activities and the weekend warrior at the top)
weekly_ranges.cod_cuts: 0-56 (court activities and the weekend warrior at the top)

share_of_weekly_sets_in_these_profiles.note: The coach's own weekend-warrior template was about 32 % athletic sets in 04 v1 (40 of 124); with the v1.1 resistance block (R2-SES-05, 2-4 exercises per muscle group) it is about 25 %; endurance and 60+ profiles sit lower, court and youth profiles higher (computed)

dial.scale: 0 none - 1 a little - 2 regular - 3 leads the plan (analyst summary, PROPOSED)

what_it_is_not: not competitive: no position, no season start date, no pre-season or in-season blocks (COACH-ANSWER GEN-02)
no contrast / French-contrast complexes by default - they are for L2+ athletes in an off-season (COACH-ANSWER ATH-12; gen-pop reading INFERRED)
not aesthetics: medball throws stay in the main workout (ATH-05 removes them only for aesthetics)
no 1RM or max-mile tests from zero (COACH-R2 PER-07)
no lifestyle questions (sleep, stress, job) - workouts only (COACH-R2 GEN-04)
stay_athletic_standard.play_days: play / activity days are entered like practice or game days: hardest gym day >= 48 h before the heaviest play day; weeks with 3+ play sessions drop the extra agility drills and halve the plyos; a 45-60+ min session of a moderate activity can replace up to 2 of the 3 aerobic sessions (COACH-R2 ATH-07 logic extended; 06 v1.1 R17 - PROPOSED)
stay_athletic_standard.event_date: optional (race, tournament, trip): the block's hardest weeks end 1 week before, then a 1-week taper at about half the sets (06 v1.1 event_peak_genpop - PROPOSED)
stay_athletic_standard.year: the gen-pop year stays the default and is fully user-tunable (re-order blocks, more / less cardio, e.g. a winter strength block); an activity block can be dropped where the user wants it (COACH-R2 PER-01/02)
stay_athletic_standard.no_check_in: no check-in = the plan follows its planned stairway (COACH-R2 VOL-03); a check-in uses effort, completion and pain only (COACH-R2 VOL-01 without the life column - COACH-R2 GEN-04)
stay_athletic_standard.older_60_plus: no Olympic lifts, plyos or depth jumps by default; landing drills and low ankle hops stay (05 v1.1 reading of the approved R2-ATH-08 proposal); throws, stepping, fast-concentric machine work and balance carry the 'athletic' part; the rest is an option with W_OLDER_POWER: 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means.'
stay_athletic_standard.youth: kids and teens can use it (ATH-13); floor Olympic lifts from about 14 after a hang block (COACH-R2 ATH-08); youth_general_athletic profile
stay_athletic_standard.evidence: COACH (ATH-13, ATH-10, ATH-11, ATH-07, R2-ATH-01/03/04/08, R2-SES-03/05, R2-VOL-04/06) for the parts; doses per activity PROPOSED - PENDING COACH APPROVAL

profiles.rationale: The coach asked for pickleball by name ('a very popular sport right now'). Players need lateral first steps, split-step reactions, rotation both ways, single-leg control, calves / Achilles and shoulder-elbow care. Many players are older, so the 60+ rules switch on automatically (COACH-R2 ATH-08) and falls are the main injury mechanism in seniors (G3).
science: 24.3 million US players in 2025 (16.8 M casual, 7.48 M core); +171.8 % in three years [G1, G2]
players 65+ were the second-largest age bracket (15.4 %) in SFIA's 2023 data [G2b]
seniors (>= 60) 2010-2019: strains / sprains 31.0 %, fractures 30.4 %; slip / trip / fall / dive 66.9 %; wrist and lower leg the most common sites; women 9.3 x more likely to fracture a wrist [G3]
singles and doubles reach about 70 % of predicted max heart rate in 40-85-year-olds; 6 weeks of play (3 x 60 min) improved VO2max, blood pressure and lipids [G4]
racket sports: Achilles and calf problems in masters players; 'tennis leg' (medial gastrocnemius) is typical of middle-aged recreational players [G31, G32]
confirm: Should open-play sessions replace gym aerobic sessions (up to 2 of 3)?
Pickleball's plyo share: 50 % like tennis (class 3)?

derived.derived_note: computed by the genpop builder: athletic doses with the 04 nominal reps per set (PLYO 8 contacts of which landing_pct are landings, JLK 20, BALL 5, THROW 10, COD 7, SPRINT 60 m, TE 4); resistance / core / calves = the 05 v1.1 athletic template for these days at 60 min, mid-block ('2-3' sets = 2.5); muscle sets with helpers 0.25 (VOL-09) and the R2-VOL-05 glute credits (BHD split hip-thrust day / deadlift day = 0.625 glutes + 0.625 hamstrings, INFERRED); FOCUS on optional days counted as arms (PROPOSED). The volume engine (12 v1.1) sets the real per-muscle numbers: general factor x0.8 then the floor of 10 (COACH-R2 VOL-04/06); muscles listed below the floor are lifted by the engine (longer day, supersets or the optional day - R2-SES-05). Minutes = 05 time costs (60-min column), straight sets, block start ~ this value, late block longer.
derived.minutes_note: rough upper bound: 05 v1.1 time costs (60-min column) incl. set-up time, straight sets, plus this profile's athletic stations (the 05 template checks report about 63-72 min at block start for the same resistance blocks); the coach allows longer full-body days (R2-SES-05) - superset the pairs first (ORD-05); at 45 min the 05 session-length model drops stations by its cut priority (05 session_length_model.cut_priority_when_short); general clients' usual target is 45-60 min (UNI-09)

emphasis.scale: 0 none - 1 low - 2 moderate - 3 high, from the 04 tier of the weekly dose (plyometric contacts, throws, cuts, sprint metres); a jump score of 1 with no fast-reactive contacts = low-amplitude / ballistic jumps only

training_block.stages: Receive-Create stages: 12-week plan RC1 Land wk 1-3, RC2 Land & Go wk 4-7, RC3 Repeat wk 8-12; 8-week plan 1-2 / 3-5 / 6-8; restart at stage 1 each new block series; maintenance blocks stay at the current stage; L2-L3 may start at stage 2 (COACH-R2 ATH-03); bilateral before unilateral inside each stage (CAT-10)

profiles.rationale: Padel is a fast-growing doubles racket sport (over 1 million US players in 2025). Rallies are short and frequent, with many overheads and low volleys; the elbow is the most injured site, then knee, shoulder and low back (G5). Same frame as recreational pickleball with more overhead and forward-back work.
science: injury incidence about 3 per 1000 h of training and 8 per 1000 matches; elbow most common, then knee, shoulder, low back; tendon 44-49 %, muscle 27-34 % (mean ages 31-57) [G5]
match play: heart rate about 70-80 % of max, rallies mostly 3-15 s, work : rest about 0.84, low glycolytic contribution [G6]
1.07 million Americans played padel in 2025; about 1,000 US courts by April 2026, Florida about 41 % of courts [G7]

profiles.rationale: The coach named HYROX ('high rows') as something gen-pop people want to do. The race is 8 x 1 km runs, each followed by a station (SkiErg 1000 m, sled push 50 m, sled pull 50 m, burpee broad jumps 80 m, row 1000 m, farmers carry 200 m, sandbag lunges 100 m, wall balls 100). Aerobic capacity is the main predictor; strength must be enough to move the Open loads. The coach already mentions HYROX twice in round 1 (EQ-06 heavier ball for wall balls, VOL-11 40-rep sets).
science: race format and Open weights: sled push 152 / 102 kg incl. sled, sled pull 103 / 78 kg, farmers 2 x 24 / 2 x 16 kg, sandbag 20 / 10 kg, wall ball 6 / 4 kg (men / women) [G8]

about 86.5 min at about 79.5 % of max heart rate; VO2max, lower body fat and endurance-training volume predicted time; grip strength and resistance-training volume did not; recommended resistance : endurance training about 1 : 1 to 1 : 2 [G9]
running takes about half the race time (practitioner analysis) [G37]; HYROX = aerobic base + anaerobic power + local muscular endurance + strength (review) [G10]
survey (preprint): about half of HYROX athletes reported an injury; knee most common (20.8 %), mostly gradual tendon complaints; more HYROX-specific sessions per week = more injuries (OR 1.61) [G11]
confirm: HYROX: 4 aerobic sessions (A + B + C + a second C) with 2 station circuits as finishers?
HYROX plyo share 50 % (class 3 'mixed')?
Are station circuits counted as muscle sets? (proposed: no - conditioning)

profiles.rationale: Running is one of the most popular US activities (over 50 million). New runners get hurt more per hour than experienced ones (G13), so the gym part builds strength, calves / Achilles and reactive stiffness while the runs climb gently. The coach's own endurance plan is the Chris Hinshaw half marathon, used as-is (PRG-12).
science: novice runners 17.8 injuries per 1000 h vs 7.7 for recreational runners; most injuries at the knee and lower leg [G13]
high-load, plyometric and combined strength training improve running economy (systematic review with meta-analysis) [G15]
Couch to 5K: 3 runs a week for 9 weeks, run / walk progression [G14]

rules: rows >= presses, rear delts and KB face pulls every week (VOL-17, R2-LIB-04); thoracic extension mobility in the warm-up
back extensions / reverse hyper on the non-axial hinge day (R2-SES-01/02); core anti-flexion holds
hip-flexor length and glute work (hip thrust on the non-axial day) to balance the flexed riding position
anterior knee pain: slow quad work and isometrics (ISO_QUAD) and a bike-fit check with a professional (saddle height) - INFERRED
hands / wrists: grip and forearm work (ISO_GRIP); no extra loaded wrist extension if numbness is reported
keep the plan's jump and landing work (ballistic box / squat jumps, ankle hops, stick-the-landing) - for these activities it is also bone loading (PROPOSED)
heavy compound strength 2x/week (squat or leg press, deadlift or hinge) - floor of 10 sets per muscle (COACH-R2 VOL-04/06)
PROPOSED for coach approval: an optional 2-3-minute 'impact snack' (ankle hops / jump rope) on ride or swim days for users under 60 without osteoporosis or a fracture history
60+ or osteoporosis / fracture history: moderate impact only (landing drills, low ankle hops - COACH-R2 ATH-08 default) + progressive resistance (G30)
the first 2-3 classes are done at an easy-to-moderate effort (about 5-6 out of 10), seated, with low resistance, and the user stops at unusual muscle pain
dark urine, severe muscle pain or weakness after a class = see a doctor (safety copy for the product, LEGAL REVIEW)
class count adds to the plan's aerobic sessions; more classes = fewer gym aerobic sessions (COACH-R2 SES-06 adjustable)
prefer DB/KB neutral grips over front-rack barbell for strikers
limit front-squat rack volume when wrist pain flagged
COACH-ANSWER VOL-03: cut that muscle or pattern 30-50%, move it to machines or split grips, keep it moving - or drop the exercise altogether if it is too much

swap fixed-grip barbell/bar -> DB/KB/handles in the same pattern; swap bilateral -> unilateral in the same pattern (MASTER_MODEL athletic A6); keep the sets ideally, 'but you have to adjust accordingly' (UNI-08)
pain moves the bilateral : unilateral share (UNI-02)
'Felt a PAIN' -> swap within the category or lower the level (GEN-05 RIGHT); if twice in a slot: swap, then cut sets, then drop a library level (INFERRED order)
all prehab uses DB, KB, cable, machine, bodyweight or plates - never bands or variable resistance (COACH-ANSWER EQ-01, EQ-12)

profiles.rationale: Skiers and snowboarders ski a few weeks a year and get hurt when their legs fatigue. Prep builds eccentric / isometric quads, lateral strength, landing control and Green-interval fitness, peaks before the first trip and holds through the season.
science: knee = about one-third of recreational alpine ski injuries; the ACL is the most often injured structure in knee injuries needing hospitalisation [G22]
snowboarders: wrist injuries about 18-22 % (vs about 5 % in skiers); patterns stable since 1999 [G23]
a day of recreational skiing leaves eccentric quadriceps and hamstring fatigue lasting >= 24 h; eccentric pre-season training is recommended [G24]

Wed - S2 (medball + hip + push; snatch day): warm-up 5 min any cardio + A-drills / mobility (ORD-08, not volume) -> core 2 exercises x 2 sets, light, short of failure (R2-SES-03; movable - ATH-11) -> medball throws -> box jump stick -> snatch variant -> NON-AXIAL HINGE (hip thrust / back extension / reverse hyper, R2-SES-01) + horizontal push -> single-leg hinge + vertical push -> chest fly or push-up variant + side / rear delts -> calves 2 exercises

open_questions.topic: Does the activity count as aerobic?
open_questions.detail: Proposed: a moderate session of 45-60+ min (open-play pickleball, a padel or tennis match, walking golf, a hike, a ride, a swim, a class) replaces one of the 3 aerobic sessions, at most 2. ATH-07 fixes the count (3) but not what counts.

open_questions.topic: Floor of 10 sets per muscle on 2-day plans
open_questions.detail: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06 ('nobody needs less than 10'). Runners, cyclists, swimmers and dance-class users are planned at 2 gym days; at 60 min the 05 2-day template leaves several muscles below 10 at mid-block (see derived.muscles_below_floor_10_at_mid_block). The engine lifts them (longer days, supersets, optional day). Alternative: treat the activity's own work as partial credit (e.g. swimming for lats). Needs a coach rule.

open_questions.topic: Recreational profiles: the activity's class or the weekend-warrior 50 %?
open_questions.detail: COACH-R2 ATH-01 approved weekend warriors 50 %. sports/team.json gives every rec_* team sport 50 %. This file uses the activity's own class where its contact time clearly differs (golf / hiking / surf = 25 %; swimming / cycling / ski / kickball = 40 %, matching the competitive swimming, cycling and alpine-ski classes in sports/aquatic-endurance-track.json; running = 75 %), following the coach's rule that contact time sets the share (ATH-01). The merge should pick one convention.

05 v1.1 keeps landing drills and low ankle hops by default (the approved R2-ATH-08 proposal); the coach's added words say no plyos by default. This file keeps landing drills and low ankle hops, plus light medball throws and EASY-TURN reactive stepping (not plyos - INFERRED). Depth jumps: EQ-03 says never; R2-ATH-08's text lists them among the optional items. This file keeps them OFF even with the opt-in and never offers snatch variants (EQ-03).

HYROX is not on the coach's approved class or aerobic lists. Proposed: class 3 (50 %), 4 aerobic sessions (A + B + C + a second C, like the approved aesthetics second Orange), 2 station circuits a week as density work not counted as muscle sets, wall balls with the race ball (EQ-06 exception).

open_questions.topic: Light footwork station for golf, HYROX and hiking
open_questions.detail: The 'stay athletic' wording asks for some agility; these activities need none. Proposed: one EASY-TURN footwork station a week (2 sets).

06 v1.1 proposes an optional event date for gen pop (race, tournament, trip) with a 1-week taper at about half the sets. The coach approved the 1-2-week taper for competitive athletes (R2-PER-06), not yet for gen pop.

open_questions.topic: Bone-loading 'impact snack' for cyclists and swimmers
open_questions.detail: ESSA suggests about 50 impacts a session several days a week for bone (G30); the plan gives about 60-80 jump and hop contacts a week in the gym. Proposed: an optional 2-3-min ankle-hop / jump-rope snack on ride or swim days (under 60, no osteoporosis).

open_questions.topic: Kickball and other unresearched rec sports
open_questions.detail: No peer-reviewed kickball data were found; hotspots and class are INFERRED from softball. HYROX injury data come from a 2026 preprint (G11).

That file also defines rec_swimming, rec_cycling and rec_ski_snowboard (weekend-warrior 50 % convention). The intake (generator_spec v1.1 F11r) points to lap_swim, cycling_fitness and ski_snow_prep in this file. Proposed: keep the F11r ids from this file, fold the sibling's extra injury codes (KNEE_MEDIAL_KICK, LOW_BACK_EXTENSION, FALL_UPPER_LIMB, PATELLOFEMORAL_ITB) into them, and alias SHOULDER_SWIMMER_PADDLER / BONE_LOW_IMPACT to SHOULDER_SWIMMER / BONE_LOADING_NON_IMPACT.

All name_es values are PROPOSED neutral Latin American Spanish with English gym words in brackets (COACH-R2 GEN-08) and need the coach's line-by-line approval; 'pickleball', 'kickball', 'HYROX' and 'flag football' stay in English (no common Spanish name).
